note: Pinned benchmark configuration. Acceptance numbers are only comparable when this file is used unchanged; every run and every fixture records it.

rigid_init.note: Closed-form Kabsch fit over the landmark correspondences: no sampling and no iteration, so a prepared case is reproducible run to run. The 'icp' method is kept for comparison only (its surface sampling is not seedable, so it is not reproducible).

gates.note: Acceptance is anchored on the recorded reference baseline: per pair the native solver must stay within the tolerances below of the best result the reference implementation reached on that pair. The absolute targets are reported for context only - the reference implementation itself does not reach them on every pair, which is why they are not gates.

amberg.note: steps are (smoothness, landmark weight, normal weight, max iterations); this is the tuned schedule that reaches the documented numbers, and the landmark column is what makes or breaks the result

sumner.note: null keeps the library's default schedule, whose landmark weight is 1000

solver.note: Schedule of the native solver. It is deliberately not part of the configuration fingerprint: the reference baseline means the same thing whatever our own schedule is. Status: under tuning. Tuned with bench/experiments/schedule_sweep.py; measured over the four pairs by bench/compare_to_reference.py: cat0->cat3 corr_mean 1.69 (better than the reference's 2.07, but foldover 1.38% against 1.32% allowed), david0->david1 3.00 against 3.05 (passes), michael0->michael2 2.51 against 3.22 (passes, better than the reference), victoria0->victoria2 2.38 against 2.05 (16% over; stretch 0.439 against 0.435). Levers still untested: more levels, more inner iterations, the slope filter, and a per-pair look at the landmark schedule.
